nodes.title: kon/name figures are built from their five angle sizes: every two at least 10° apart on a 5° grid (gate 1 asks 8°), the two joined rays given the lengths that make the triangle's corners (VX : VY = sin cY : sin cX, at least 12 units apart), the third ray its own length; anglesApart checks the figure as drawn, so find's '≠' row is true read as 'another angle' or as 'not equal'. Reverse if: a figure family is needed whose sizes cannot be 8° apart (then replace '≠' with a mark that claims no size).

kon/name find draws its key arc (and its joined pair) once per request, evenly over the five arcs, and every figure the picker sees has that key: the key is each arc 1 time in 5 as served (the picker's scoring cannot tilt it), the wide arc included, the vertex angle outside the triangle as often as the one inside. The wide-arc key is exempt from the read-across refusal (it is over 90°, and any angle over 90° has its vertex between its arms' ends by rows or columns), so reading across wins exactly on those levels, 1 in 5. A key whose first-letter reading is not drawn (wide, outside) has no mal acts. Reverse if: judges hold reading across on wide-arc levels as a shortcut (then serve the wide arc as a key only with a non-text layout, or drop it and weight the first tap at 1 in 4).

kon/name find after gate 1, 600 picker requests (fades 1-3, seeds 20000-20599): keys by arc 138/119/119/110/114; a first tap by 'a corner arc' wins 0.187, 'an arc inside the triangle' 0.197, 'the widest' 0.198, 'the smallest angle' 0.213, 'one of the three smallest' 0.267 (the size floor: vertex keys are kept under 65° so reading across never finds them). Picker CPU over 60 requests (seeds 700-729): p50 2.9 ms, p95 15.6 ms, max 22.7 (bar 50; before gate 1 the same blocks measured p95 15-21).
